sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Sevier County?
sections.html:
Three offices split the job, and all of them work out of the Sevier County Courthouse at 125 Court Avenue in Sevierville. One values the land and buildings, the County Commission chooses the rate, and the Trustee prints the bills and collects. Knowing which desk answers which question saves walking between floors.

  • Property Assessor: Suite 210 West, voice 865.453.3242, weekdays from 8 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon. The staff appraise, classify and assess taxable property and update ownership and tax maps from recorded deeds.
  • Trustee: Room 212W, telephone (865) 453-2767, on the same schedule. Walk in through the west-end doors and it is the first office on your right. A payment drop box stands behind the courthouse, where the 30 minute parking area meets West Bruce Street.
  • Clerk and Master: Suite 108 W, (865) 453-4654. Delinquent accounts end up here, and so does the annual tax sale auction.

The county's Property Assessor page makes clear that rate-setting belongs to the Commission. Sevierville, Pigeon Forge and Gatlinburg sit inside the county, so ask the city hall where your house stands whether a separate city bill exists.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Sevier County itself?
sections.html:
Sevier County spreads over 598 square miles along the northern edge of the Great Smoky Mountains, and Sevierville anchors it as the seat of government. Roughly thirty percent of the national park falls inside the county lines, and visitor spending drives the local economy. Gatlinburg and Pigeon Forge offer Ripley's Aquarium of the Smokies, Ober Gatlinburg and Dollywood, and cabin rentals have multiplied alongside them. A single school district, Sevier County Schools, covers every address.

The Assessor runs an online filing for nightly rentals, and the county posts a short-term rental tax estimator beside its primary home and vacant land estimator. Census Bureau QuickFacts for Sevier County reports:

  • 101,342 people as of July 2025, a 2.7% gain over the April 2020 base
  • 62,724 housing units, and 70.7% of households own their home (2020 to 2024)
  • $299,000 typical value for homes lived in by their owners
  • $62,581 median household income, with 13.2% of people in poverty
  • 1,139 building permits during 2025

sections.h2: How is a Sevier County property tax bill figured?
sections.html:
Tennessee takes the appraised value, applies a ratio fixed by state law, and multiplies the result by the local rate. The State Comptroller's tax bill guide puts residential and farm land at one quarter of appraised value and commercial or industrial land at 40 percent. Rates are stated for each hundred dollars of assessed value.

Take a house appraised at $300,000. Its assessed value is $75,000. Using the $1.48 listed in the Trustee's FAQ for 2024, the yearly tax would be $1,110. That is only an illustration, because Sevier County reappraises on a five-year cycle and 2026 is a reappraisal year. The county's statement on reappraisal notices says the Assessor must review roughly 90,000 parcels, a certified rate is then calculated under state law to hold total collections steady, and the Board of Commissioners adopts the final figure. Some owners will see higher bills and some lower, so read the 2026 bill itself.

Between cycles, values stay where they are unless the property physically changes. A change in ownership alone does not move the assessment.

sections.h2: What are the Sevier County payment dates for this season?
sections.html:
The 2026 bills were mailed in early October and can be paid from October 1 onward without penalty, through the end of February 2027. This mid-November week falls inside that window. After the deadline, interest of 1.5 percent accrues every month on the unpaid base amount. Checks sent by mail must carry a postmark dated no later than that last day, since the Trustee refuses office meter dates, and card or e-check payments count on the day of the transaction. Partial payments are welcome, and only the leftover balance collects interest.

The Trustee does not copy mortgage companies, so a homeowner with an escrow account should pass the bill along. Each year's tax covers that calendar year.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Sevier County assessment?
sections.html:
Call the Assessor first, then carry the dispute to the Board of Equalization if the answer falls short. The county's reappraisal statement gives the Assessor's reappraisal line as (865) 774-3756, staffed weekday mornings and afternoons, plus reappraisal@seviercountytn.gov. It also tells anyone who thinks a value is wrong that an appeal can be filed with that board, which begins hearing appeals June 1.

Pull together evidence before you call: recent sales of similar houses, repair estimates for defects the appraisal missed, and facts about square footage or condition. Ask the Assessor's office for the filing deadline in the current cycle, since notice dates shift. Do not wait for the bill to arrive before you start.

sections.h2: What property tax relief is available in Sevier County?
sections.html:
The Trustee administers two state programs for homeowners, and staff complete the application with you at the counter. Tax Relief covers all or part of the tax on a home, mobile homes included, for people 65 or older, the disabled, disabled veterans, and widows or widowers of disabled veterans. Posted figures for 2025 taxes:

  • Elderly and disabled owners: household income capped at $37,530 including a spouse, with relief figured on market value up to $32,700
  • Disabled veterans and their surviving spouses: no income test, relief figured on market value up to $175,000
  • Tax Freeze, age 65 and up: income may not exceed $47,990 for 2024, and the application is renewed each year

Relief reaches city taxes too. Greenbelt is a separate break for parcels of 15 acres or more in farm or forestry use, requested by March 1; land that drops out owes a rollback of the taxes saved over the last three years. Ask the Trustee for the limits that apply this year before you plan around these figures.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Sevier County tax when I sell?
sections.html:
The tax lien follows the parcel, so any balance must be cleared at or before closing. The Trustee mails each bill to whoever is listed as owner, and its FAQ tells new buyers to read the closing statement to learn who handles that year's tax. The title company ordinarily settles any open balance at the table.

If a bill is not paid by the deadline, the account turns delinquent and moves to Chancery Court, where costs are added and the parcel can be advertised for the yearly auction. The Clerk and Master publishes the list 20 to 30 days ahead, bidders register in person half an hour before the sale starts, and payment is cash, money order or check. The former owner has a year to redeem, and the bidder earns 1 percent per month in the meantime. Anyone with a delinquent account should phone the Trustee at (865) 453-2767 before the list appears.

faqs.q: Who mails the property tax bill in Sevier County?
faqs.a: The Trustee does, normally in the first week of October. The Assessor values the property and the County Commission picks the rate, but only the Trustee at 125 Court Avenue, Room 212W, collects. Call (865) 453-2767 if no bill shows up.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for paying Sevier County property tax without interest?
faqs.a: The final day of February. For the 2026 bill, that is February 2027. Beginning March 1, interest runs at 1.5 percent monthly (18 percent yearly), and a late postmark counts as a late payment.

faqs.q: Can I pay Sevier County property tax in pieces?
faqs.a: Yes, the Trustee accepts partial payments, and interest builds only on whatever remains once the account is delinquent. Owners 65 or older may also qualify for state Tax Relief or Tax Freeze, both handled in person at the Trustee's office.

faqs.q: How often does Sevier County reappraise?
faqs.a: Every five years, with 2026 as the current reappraisal year. The Assessor's page explains that values hold between cycles unless the property physically changes. After reappraisal, a certified rate is calculated so total collections stay steady.

faqs.q: Will an unpaid Sevier County tax bill stop a sale?
faqs.a: It will not stop the sale, but the balance has to come from sale money because the lien stays on the parcel. Ask the Trustee what the exact payoff is on your closing date. Accounts sent to Chancery Court pick up costs and can end in a tax sale.
